files.prompt:
Use case: historical-scene / game interface background.
Create ONE finished, full-bleed, wide 16:9 landscape background texture for the Chinese historical naval strategy game "Ming Armada". Desired canvas 2560 x 1440. It will sit UNDER real interactive interface text and buttons; deliver background art ONLY.
References: Image 1 is the PRIMARY MATERIAL reference: the user's worn pale brown fibrous paper/cloth, irregular age spots, scuffed patches, imperfect fiber edges. Use its tactile surface language without reproducing the hanging sheets, building or low-resolution blur. Image 2 is SECONDARY WORLD/MATERIAL reference: late-Ming wooden Chinese junks, battened tan sails, weathered timber, gray-blue sea and naturalistic historical texture. DO NOT COPY any people, cannon foreground, flags, specific composition, mountain buildings or active battle.

Art direction: an authentic-feeling old mariner's chart sheet made from warm tan, heavy handmade paper with a subtle kraft/leather-like patina, dusty ivory rubbed areas and gentle tea-brown aging. A beautiful usable screen background, quiet and premium, old and tactile yet legible. Fine irregular cellulose fibers visible; broad, soft irregular tonal variations. Slight rubbed and flaking paper layers are concentrated around the perimeter like the supplied reference. Smooth, calm, softly illuminated center, neither a flat digital gradient nor grungy dirt. The sheet fills the entire canvas edge to edge; no table beneath, no perspective tilt, no curled scroll rollers, no obvious rectangular frame, no border, no drop shadow.

Naval/Ming character: near the bottom left corner a restrained ink-and-earth-pigment drawing of two late-Ming Chinese sailing junks with battened sails and convincingly weathered hulls, subtle dimensional brushwork echoing the novel illustrations; their low-contrast wakes merge into pale ink-blue waves along the very bottom. Along the far right and upper right edge, faint schematic coastal contours, a small old stone harbor and a few washed-out distant sails, treated as hand-drawn chart fragments IN the paper. A few extremely faint navigation arcs and dotted route marks near edges only, no Western fantasy compass rose, no real map claims. Uneven faded ink and tiny dry-brush accents, all cohesive on ONE sheet, not a collage or divided panels. Main ships occupy at most the outer left 20% and bottom 22%, never huge hero objects.

UI readability is essential: keep the central 60% of width and 65% of height clear of ships, coastlines, strong folds, stains, black marks or ornaments. Keep the upper-center area similarly quiet for a title. Main menu labels and large UI panels must remain easy to read over it. Any high-frequency detail is confined to the extreme edges and lower corners. Palette: warm uncoated parchment beige, ochre-brown, faded sepia, very restrained ink-blue/teal at edges, a tiny muted cinnabar dab at most; absolutely no bright gold, glossy metal, neon or dark vignette.
No people. No baked-in UI, buttons, boxes, icons, grids, headings, logos, watermark, Chinese characters, pseudo-calligraphy, readable letters or numbers. No Qing symbols or queues, no European pirate skulls, no steamships, no modern paper print or 3D fantasy ornament. Soft diffuse light, mature understated historical painting blended into physically convincing aged paper. One seamless-looking continuous background, sharp high resolution, wide 16:9.
